title: Bill Green's Kansas City 7 playing his tune "See You Later, So Long"
summary: He heard the group play his tune on the radio, which he recorded as "Dedicated to the Blues", and praises its performance.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Well, we're becoming more and more Callender conscious here lately. I've noticed your name more and more often. A week ago Bill Green's Kansas City 7 broadcast live from the County Museum, and they played Red Callender originals.

I heard it. And I taped it. I wrote them a thank-you note. That's one of the tunes I was telling you about some time ago. It originally started as 'Dolphin Street Boogie,' and then I made a record on it... I said I was copying Duke Ellington. I did a record on it, and called it 'Dedicated To the Blues.' And now with the new title, we call it 'See You Later, So Long.' It now has a lyric.
Oh, that's the one that Mary Lou...
Mary Lou wrote a great lyric to it.
I didn't realize that was the same... When I heard the instrumental version on the radio, I didn't realize it was the same one.
"I'll See You Later, So Long." That's the same one.
Of course. Well, Bill's group did a magnificent job.
Yes, I thought it was very well done.
I also thought the group was nice.
